parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: The equation shown in (a)(i) describes the reaction which occurs when aqueous potassium iodide is added to aqueous copper(II) sulfate. A white precipitate of copper(I) iodide forms in a brown solution of iodine and potassium sulfate.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text:
Balance the equation and include state symbols.

$$\ldots\ldots\text{CuSO}_{4}(\ldots\ldots) + \ldots\ldots\text{KI}(\ldots\ldots) \rightarrow \ldots\ldots\text{CuI}(\ldots\ldots) + \ldots\ldots\text{I}_{2}(\ldots\ldots) + \ldots\ldots\text{K}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}(\ldots\ldots)$$

The table gives the oxidation numbers of iodine in the different species in the equation.

| iodine-containing species | oxidation number of iodine |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{KI}$ | $-1$ |
| $\text{CuI}$ | $-1$ |
| $\text{I}_{2}$ | $0$ |

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Deduce the oxidation number of copper in $\text{CuSO}_{4}$ and $\text{CuI}$.

- oxidation number of copper in $\text{CuSO}_{4}$

- oxidation number of copper in $\text{CuI}$

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe the type of reaction shown by the equation in (a)(i). Explain your answer in terms of electron transfer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
In the reaction described in (a)(i), a student uses $17.43\text{ g}$ of $\text{CuSO}_{4}\cdot\mathbf{y}\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. By further titration of the reaction products the student concludes that the total amount of $\text{CuSO}_{4}$ in the sample is $0.0982\text{ mol}$.

Use the Data Booklet to complete the table to calculate the value of $\mathbf{y}$, where $\mathbf{y}$ is an integer. Show your working.

| mass of $0.0982\text{ mol CuSO}_{4}$ | g |
| :--- | :--- |
| amount of $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ in $17.43\text{ g}$ of $\text{CuSO}_{4}\cdot\mathbf{y}\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ | $\text{mol H}_{2}\text{O}$ |
| value of $\mathbf{y}$ |  |
